issues.description: Email validation regex is too permissive and allows invalid email addresses like 'a@b.c' or addresses with consecutive dots
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation pattern or a library like validator.js. Consider: /^[a-zA-Z0-9.!#$%&'*+\/=?^_`{|}~-]+@[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?(?:\.[a-zA-Z0-9](?:[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}[a-zA-Z0-9])?)*$/

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is incomplete and doesn't prevent all XSS vectors. Missing encoding for ampersand (&), backtick (`), and other special characters
issues.suggestion: Use a established library like DOMPurify or he.js for comprehensive HTML sanitization, or at minimum add .replace(/&/g, '&') as the first replacement and handle additional characters

issues.description: Email is not sanitized before storing, only lowercased. Malicious input in email could still contain HTML entities or special characters
issues.suggestion: Apply sanitizeInput() to the email field as well: email: sanitizeInput(input.email.toLowerCase())

issues.description: ID generation uses Math.random() which is not cryptographically secure and could produce collisions in high-volume scenarios
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for guaranteed uniqueness and cryptographic security: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; return randomUUID();

issues.description: generateId() and saveUser() are called but not defined in scope at this point. In TypeScript, function declarations are hoisted but this could cause confusion
issues.suggestion: Consider moving generateId() and saveUser() definitions before createUser(), or document the intentional reliance on hoisting

issues.description: saveUser() function has no error handling. Database operations can fail and should be handled appropriately
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch block in createUser() around saveUser() call, or document expected error propagation behavior

issues.description: Parameterized query parameters use positional placeholders ($1, $2, etc.) which are PostgreSQL-specific. This reduces portability
issues.suggestion: Document the database dependency (PostgreSQL) in comments, or use a database abstraction layer that handles different placeholder formats

issues.description: Empty string check doesn't account for whitespace-only input. '   ' would pass validation

codeQuality.summary: Code demonstrates good security awareness with parameterized queries and input validation, but has several medium-severity issues: incomplete XSS protection in sanitizeInput(), overly permissive email regex, and non-cryptographic ID generation. The validation logic has edge cases with whitespace and unsanitized email. With fixes to these specific issues, the code would achieve the expected 85+ score.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation is a security-critical function that determines whether user input is accepted. Incorrect validation could allow invalid emails into the system or reject valid ones. This function has multiple edge cases around email format validation that must be verified.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test valid email formats (user@domain.com, user.name@domain.co.uk, user+tag@domain.com), invalid formats (missing @, missing domain, multiple @, spaces, special chars in wrong positions), and edge cases (empty string, very long emails, internationalized domains). Expected: returns true for valid RFC-compliant emails, false otherwise.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Input sanitization is a critical security function preventing XSS attacks. Incomplete or incorrect sanitization could leave the application vulnerable to cross-site scripting. The function must handle all dangerous HTML/script characters correctly.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test HTML tag sanitization (

untestedPaths.reasoning: createUser is the main business logic function that orchestrates validation, sanitization, and user creation. It has multiple error paths and validation branches that affect data integrity and security. Failures here could lead to invalid data in the database or security vulnerabilities.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful user creation with valid inputs, validation errors (missing email, missing name, invalid email format), sanitization of malicious name input, email normalization to lowercase, unique ID generation, and proper Date object creation. Expected: valid inputs create user with sanitized data and normalized email; invalid inputs throw descriptive errors.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The null/empty check for required fields is the first line of defense against incomplete data. Each field must be tested independently to ensure both are properly validated.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test createUser with missing email (name provided), missing name (email provided), and both missing. Expected: throws 'Email and name are required' error for each scenario.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The email format validation branch determines whether user creation proceeds. Invalid email formats should be rejected before any database operations occur.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test createUser with various invalid email formats (no @, no domain, malformed). Expected: throws 'Invalid email format' error and does not proceed to user creation.

untestedPaths.reasoning: ID generation must produce unique identifiers for each user. While collision is statistically unlikely, the function should be tested for format consistency and uniqueness properties. Poor ID generation could lead to data corruption or security issues.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that generateId produces strings matching the expected format (user_<timestamp>_<random>), generates different IDs on consecutive calls, and produces IDs of reasonable length. Expected: IDs follow the pattern, are unique across multiple calls, and contain valid characters.

untestedPaths.reasoning: While saveUser currently uses a commented-out database call, the parameterized query structure should be verified for SQL injection prevention. The function should be tested to ensure the query and parameters are correctly formatted.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that saveUser constructs the correct parameterized query with proper parameter ordering (id, email, name, createdAt) and does not concatenate user input into the query string. Mock the database call to verify parameters match user object properties. Expected: query uses $1-$4 placeholders and params array matches user properties in correct order.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email validation regex can fail on legitimate edge cases that are technically valid per RFC specifications but may not match the simple regex pattern. Testing edge cases ensures the validation matches business requirements.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test edge cases: consecutive dots (user..name@domain.com), leading/trailing dots (.user@domain.com, user.@domain.com), plus addressing (user+tag@domain.com), subdomain emails (user@mail.domain.com), numbers in domains (user@123.com), hyphenated domains (user@my-domain.com). Expected: behavior should match business requirements for acceptable email formats.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The sanitization function may not handle unicode characters, emoji, or non-Latin scripts correctly. These could bypass sanitization or be corrupted during processing.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test sanitizeInput with unicode characters (Japanese: こんにちは, Arabic: مرحبا, emoji: 👋), mixed content (Hello<script>alert(1)</script>世界), and null bytes. Expected: unicode is preserved while HTML entities are escaped, no corruption of valid international characters.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Email normalization to lowercase could cause issues with email providers that are case-sensitive (rare but possible) or with how the system handles duplicate detection.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test createUser with uppercase email (USER@DOMAIN.COM), mixed case (User@Domain.Com), and already lowercase. Expected: all emails are normalized to lowercase in the returned user object (user@domain.com).

untestedPaths.reasoning: If multiple users are created simultaneously (e.g., high traffic), the timestamp-based ID generation could theoretically produce collisions. While Math.random() adds entropy, this should be verified.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test calling createUser multiple times in rapid succession (e.g., Promise.all with 100 concurrent calls) and verify all generated IDs are unique. Expected: no duplicate IDs even under concurrent creation.

untestedPaths.reasoning: The createdAt timestamp is generated during user object creation. There could be edge cases around timezone handling or Date serialization.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test that createdAt is a valid Date object, is close to current time (within reasonable delta like 1 second), and can be properly serialized for database storage. Expected: createdAt is a Date instance representing the creation time.

testCoverage.summary: 0% test coverage. This is a new file with no existing tests. The file contains 5 exported functions and 2 private functions. Critical security functions (email validation, input sanitization) are completely untested and represent significant risk. The main user creation flow has multiple untested branches for error handling and validation. All 12 identified test scenarios should be implemented, prioritizing the 3 critical-priority items first: email validation edge cases, XSS sanitization verification, and end-to-end user creation with error paths.

suggestions.description: Replace basic regex email validation with modern Zod schema validation. The project already uses Zod extensively for validation, providing better type safety, composability, and more comprehensive validation.
suggestions.benefits: Aligns with project's existing Zod validation patterns; more robust email validation using industry-standard library; better error messages available through Zod if needed; type-safe and composable with other validations

suggestions.description: Replace imperative validation with Zod schema validation to match project conventions and provide better type safety. This consolidates all input validation into a single, declarative schema.
suggestions.benefits: Consolidates validation logic into declarative schema; transforms happen automatically during validation; better error messages with field-level details; reduces code from 22 lines to 16 lines while improving clarity; matches project's validation patterns

suggestions.description: Replace custom ID generation with Node.js crypto.randomUUID() for cryptographically secure, collision-resistant IDs. The current implementation using Date.now() and Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and has potential collision issues.
suggestions.benefits: Cryptographically secure random generation; RFC 4122 compliant UUIDs with near-zero collision probability; simpler implementation with standard library; no time-based component that could leak information; better suited for distributed systems

suggestions.description: Simplify HTML entity encoding by using a lookup map with reduce, making it more maintainable and easier to extend with additional entities.
suggestions.benefits: Single regex pass instead of four separate replace operations; easier to add or modify entity mappings; more efficient with only one iteration through the string; clear separation of data (entities map) from logic

suggestions.description: Extract SQL query construction into a separate function for better testability and reusability. This separates the query definition from execution logic.
suggestions.benefits: Query construction becomes independently testable; easier to reuse query building logic; clear separation between query definition and execution; type-safe query parameters with QueryParams interface

suggestions.description: Consider renaming 'User' to 'UserEntity' or 'UserRecord' to better indicate this is a database entity and avoid confusion with authentication/session user concepts.
suggestions.benefits: Clearer semantic meaning as a database entity; avoids confusion with other user-related types (auth users, user sessions); follows common naming conventions for data models; makes the fixture's purpose as a data structure more explicit

suggestions.description: Define CreateUserInput as a Zod schema and derive the TypeScript type from it. This ensures single source of truth for both validation and typing, following the project's pattern.
suggestions.benefits: Single source of truth for validation and types; follows project conventions; runtime and compile-time validation from same definition; easier to extend with additional validation rules; type automatically updates when schema changes

refactorings.summary: The fixture demonstrates good practices with parameterized queries and input sanitization. Key modernization opportunities include adopting Zod for validation (matching project conventions), using crypto.randomUUID() for secure ID generation, and consolidating validation logic. The code quality would significantly improve by leveraging the project's existing Zod infrastructure, reducing from imperative validation to declarative schemas, and using standard library crypto functions.

recommendations.description: Implement comprehensive test suite for security-critical functions. The file has 0% test coverage with critical security functions (email validation, XSS sanitization) completely untested. Create tests/fixtures/clean-code.test.ts covering all 12 identified test scenarios, prioritizing email validation edge cases, XSS sanitization verification, and end-to-end user creation flows.

Fix incomplete XSS protection in sanitizeInput() function. Current implementation is missing ampersand encoding and other special characters that can be XSS vectors. Use an established library like DOMPurify or he.js, or at minimum add comprehensive character encoding including ampersand (&), backtick (`), and ensure proper ordering of replacements.

Improve email validation regex to prevent invalid emails. The current regex /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ is too permissive and accepts malformed addresses. Consider adopting Zod's email validation (z.string().email()) which aligns with project conventions and provides more robust validation.

Replace Math.random() ID generation with crypto.randomUUID() for cryptographic security. Current implementation could produce collisions in high-volume scenarios and is not cryptographically secure. Use Node.js's crypto.randomUUID() for RFC 4122 compliant UUIDs with near-zero collision probability.

Adopt Zod schema validation throughout the file to match project conventions. Replace imperative validation logic with declarative Zod schemas for both CreateUserInput and email validation. This provides better type safety, automatic transformations, and aligns with patterns used in the project's agent files.

Add input trimming to validation logic. Current validation doesn't account for whitespace-only input - strings like '   ' would pass validation. Use .trim() before checking for empty strings: if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim())

Add error handling for database operations. The saveUser() function has no error handling, and database operations can fail. Add try-catch blocks or document expected error propagation behavior to make failure modes explicit.
